title: Development of a Large-Scale Pathogen Screening Test for Canine Stem Cells
author: Pekker, Priskin, et al.
materials: Positive controls — represented by target-sequence-containing plasmids — were used to optimize and validate each pathogen testing assay. All plasmids contained the target sequence for the pathogen of interest with the primer and probe-binding sites. These plasmids containing the artificial DNA fragments for each pathogen were synthesized by Twist Bioscience (San Francisco, CA), except for the Mycoplasma species, which were all cloned in the pBluescript plasmid. All the synthesized plasmids were sequenced to confirm the presence of the specific target sequence. DNA concentration was quantified using Qubit® 3.0 Fluorometer (Invitrogen) and the Qubit® dsDNA HS Assay Kit (Life Technologies), and the DNA copy number was calculated using the following formula:

Total viral nucleic acid from stem cell samples was extracted using 5 × 105 cells/MSC batch and additionally 100 μl of the corresponding cell supernatant in the case of the nine batches of uncertain purity. Isolation was performed using the MagCore® Viral Nucleic Acid Extraction Kit (RBC Bioscience, Taiwan) following the manufacturer’s recommendation. The final sample was eluted in 100 μl elution buffer. RNA concentration was measured using the Qubit™ RNA High Sensitivity Assay Kit (Invitrogen by Thermo Fisher Scientific), while the concentration of the DNA was measured using the Qubit™ dsDNA High Sensitivity Assay Kit (Invitrogen by Thermo Fisher Scientific) with a Qubit™ 3.0 fluorometer. Following total nucleic acid extraction, High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Applied Biosystems) was utilized to generate cDNA for the detection of RNA viruses. Eluted nucleic acids and synthesized cDNA were stored at − 20 °C.

For bacterial and protozoan DNA extraction, we used the QIAamp® PowerFecal® Pro DNA Kit (QIAGEN®) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. DNA was isolated using 5 × 105 cells/MSC batch and additionally 100 μl of the corresponding cell supernatant in the case of the nine batches of uncertain purity and for Mycoplasma detection in all cases. The final sample was eluted in 100 μl elution buffer. Following DNA extraction, a Qubit™ 3.0 fluorometer was used to measure DNA concentration utilizing the associated Qubit™ dsDNA High Sensitivity assay kit (Invitrogen by Thermo Fisher Scientific). Eluted DNA was stored at − 20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare and quantify positive control plasmids
steps.instruction: Obtain synthetic plasmids containing the target sequence for each pathogen (Twist Bioscience; Mycoplasma plasmids cloned in pBluescript), verify each plasmid by sequencing, quantify DNA concentration with a Qubit® 3.0 fluorometer using the Qubit® dsDNA High Sensitivity assay kit, and calculate the number of copies using the formula: Number of copies = (amount of dsDNA in ng × 6.022×10^23) / (length of dsDNA in bp × 1×10^9 × 660).

substeps.instruction: Obtain synthesized plasmids (Twist Bioscience) and Mycoplasma plasmids cloned in pBluescript.
Sequence each plasmid to confirm the presence of the specific target sequence.
Measure DNA concentration with Qubit® 3.0 fluorometer and the Qubit® dsDNA High Sensitivity assay kit.
Calculate copy number using the provided formula.

steps.title: Extract viral nucleic acids and synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: For each stem‑cell batch, use 5 × 10^5 cells (MSC) plus 100 µL supernatant for the nine batches of uncertain purity, extract total viral nucleic acid with the MagCore® Viral Nucleic Acid Extraction Kit (RBC Bioscience) following the manufacturer’s protocol, elute in 100 µL buffer, quantify RNA and DNA concentrations with Qubit™ RNA High Sensitivity and dsDNA High Sensitivity assay kits on a Qubit™ 3.0 fluorometer, reverse‑transcribe RNA to cDNA using the High‑Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Applied Biosystems), and store all eluates and cDNA at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Combine 5 × 10^5 cells per MSC batch with 100 µL supernatant for the nine uncertain‑purity batches.
Extract total viral nucleic acid using the MagCore® Viral Nucleic Acid Extraction Kit per the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute the nucleic acid in 100 µL elution buffer.
Measure RNA concentration with the Qubit™ RNA High Sensitivity Assay Kit.
Measure DNA concentration with the Qubit™ dsDNA High Sensitivity Assay Kit using a Qubit™ 3.0 fluorometer.
Generate cDNA from the extracted RNA using the High‑Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Applied Biosystems).
Store eluted nucleic acids and synthesized cDNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Extract bacterial and protozoan DNA
steps.instruction: Using the same cell input (5 × 10^5 cells per MSC batch) plus 100 µL supernatant for the nine uncertain‑purity batches and for all Mycoplasma detections, isolate bacterial and protozoan DNA with the QIAamp® PowerFecal® Pro DNA Kit (QIAGEN) according to the manufacturer’s protocol, elute in 100 µL buffer, quantify DNA with a Qubit™ 3.0 fluorometer using the dsDNA High Sensitivity assay kit, and store the DNA at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Combine 5 × 10^5 cells per MSC batch with 100 µL supernatant for the nine uncertain‑purity batches and for Mycoplasma detection.
Extract DNA using the QIAamp® PowerFecal® Pro DNA Kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Elute DNA in 100 µL elution buffer.
Measure DNA concentration with a Qubit™ 3.0 fluorometer using the dsDNA High Sensitivity assay kit.
